headline: COEUR FINDS LA PROMESA VEIN AT LAS CHISPAS — 22.6 g/t Au, 2,035 g/t Ag in Gap Zone; Los Sheiks Strike Triples to 440m (NYSE: CDE)
snippet: Coeur Mining Corp. (NYSE: CDE) released its first 2026 exploration update for Palmarejo and Las Chispas, headlined by the Gap Zone at Las Chispas where the newly confirmed La Promesa vein — located between the Augusta and William Tell veins — returned 0.4m at 22.6 g/t gold and 2,035 g/t silver, while the Los Sheiks Zone expanded from 140m to 440m along strike since 2025. Coeur's $158 million 2026 exploration budget now targets over 200,000 metres of drilling across both Mexico operations, making Las Chispas one of the most aggressively funded silver-gold near-mine discovery programs in the Americas.

headline: WESTGOLD SMASHES FY26 GUIDANCE AT 387K OZ — Record Annual Production; AUD939M Treasury; Bluebird South-Junction Hits 1Mtpa (ASX: WGX)
snippet: Westgold Resources Ltd. (ASX: WGX) reported record gold production of 387,000 ounces for FY2026 — exceeding full-year guidance with an all-in sustaining cost of A$2,841 per ounce — while Q4 cash build of A$233 million left the company with A$939 million in closing cash, bullion, and liquid investments and A$1.5 billion in total liquidity as at 30 June 2026. The company also achieved annualised mining rates beyond 1 million tonnes per annum at Bluebird South-Junction by year-end and record annual output for both its Meekatharra and Fortnum Hubs, establishing Westgold as one of Australia's most financially resilient mid-tier gold producers.

headline: LAHONTAN DRILLS 31m AT 0.90 G/T AU OXIDE — 3.25 g/t High-Grade Core in Calvada Central Permitting Holes; Nevada Heap-Leach Thesis Intact (TSXV: LG)
snippet: Lahontan Gold Corp. (TSXV: LG) reported additional 2026 drill results from the Santa Fe Mine Project in Nevada, where geotechnical permitting holes at Calvada Central intersected 30.8 metres of 0.93 g/t AuEq oxide from 94.8–125.6m downhole — including a 1.4m sub-interval of 3.25 g/t gold — confirming resource-grade oxide mineralisation even in holes designed for engineering purposes. Two additional RC holes constraining the Calvada Fault boundary have been completed with assays pending, as Lahontan advances its permitting application for a heap-leach operation at one of Nevada's most prospective near-surface oxide gold development projects.

headline: LUNDIN GOLD NOW HAS SEVEN PORPHYRIES IN ECUADOR — Sandia NE and SE Discovered; 603m at 0.68% Cu Near Surface; 2027 Maiden Resource (TSX: LUG)
snippet: Lundin Gold Inc. (TSX: LUG) announced the discovery of two additional copper-gold porphyry centres — Sandia Northeast and Sandia Southeast — adjacent to its Sandia porphyry at the Fruta del Norte district in southeast Ecuador, expanding the district total from five to seven identified systems. Drill hole SND-2025-383 cut 603 metres grading 0.68% copper from 27 metres depth in the main Sandia zone, with the multi-porphyry footprint remaining open in multiple directions and a maiden mineral resource estimate for the Sandia system targeted for early 2027.

headline: STRIKEPOINT HERCULES FINAL HOLES: 67.06m AT 0.53 G/T AU — HIGH-GRADE CORE Hits 2.93 g/t; Walker Lane Oxide Footprint Grows (TSXV: SKP)
snippet: StrikePoint Gold Inc. (TSXV: SKP) released the third and final batch of assay results from its Spring 2026 drill program at the Hercules Gold Project in Nevada's Walker Lane, with flagship hole H26005 cutting 67.06 metres grading 0.53 g/t gold and 11.69 g/t silver — including a 7.62-metre high-grade core of 2.93 g/t gold and 54.48 g/t silver — across dominantly oxide material consistent with a heap-leach development model. The 29-hole spring program expanded the SW Cliffs oxide footprint with total mineralised widths exceeding 100 metres in the best holes, and the company is now evaluating fall 2026 follow-up drilling to advance the project toward a resource estimate.

headline: GOLD HITS 2-WEEK HIGH AT $4,139 AFTER FOMC MINUTES — No Hike Signal; Silver Adds 2% to $59.87; July 29 Hold Now Priced at 97%
snippet: Spot gold climbed 1.6% to $4,139.64 per ounce on Wednesday — its highest level since July 7 — after the Federal Reserve's June FOMC minutes contained no hawkish signal, removing the near-term obstacle to gold's next upside leg with the July 29 policy decision now priced at approximately 97% hold probability. Silver added 1.9% to $59.87, approaching the $60 level for the third time this month, as the rate outlook combined with firm physical demand from South and Southeast Asia kept precious metals buyers on the bid through the session.

headline: GERMANIUM LEADS CRITICAL MINERALS SURGE: +27.8% IN JULY — Dysprosium +25.4%; ALL 18 TRACKED ELEMENTS Rise; West Pays $6,250/Kg vs $3,417 China
snippet: Every one of the 18 rare earth and critical minerals tracked by the market rose in July 2026, led by germanium at +27.8% — pushing China's domestic spot to $3,417/kg while Western buyers paid $6,250/kg, a near-2x premium driven by China's export licensing controls — and dysprosium at +25.4%, reflecting a second consecutive annual supply deficit for heavy rare earths as defence and EV demand outpaces mine output outside China. The breadth of the July rally — zero declines across all tracked elements — has not been seen since the post-COVID supply shock of 2021, with the MIIT's still-delayed H2 mining quota announcement remaining the single largest near-term catalyst for whether prices extend further or consolidate.

headline: SPROTT: URANIUM GATHERING MOMENTUM INTO Q3 2026 — $85.74/Lb Spot July 19; 79M Lb Physical Trust; Utilities Reversing Under-Contracting
snippet: Sprott Asset Management's uranium watch shows spot U3O8 at $85.74 per pound as of July 19, 2026 — holding well above the $65–$70/lb incentive pricing threshold for most tier-one development projects — as the firm's physical uranium trust has accumulated nearly 79 million pounds, one of the largest pools of physical U3O8 outside sovereign inventories. Utilities that under-contracted through 2023–2025 are re-entering the term contract market ahead of planned reactor startups in South Korea, Poland, and Japan through 2028, with Sprott flagging this returning buy-side pressure as the primary catalyst for the next leg of the uranium cycle.

headline: ED STEER: COMMERCIALS SIGNAL GOLD AND SILVER SURGE INCOMING — Short Positioning Mirrors 2024 Pre-Breakout Setup (GoldSeek)
snippet: Veteran metals commentator Ed Steer argues in his latest GoldSeek column that Commitment of Traders positioning in gold and silver futures mirrors the setup that preceded the 2024 bull market breakout, with commercial net short positions at historically compressed levels relative to open interest — a pattern Steer interprets as banks and dealers lacking the firepower to cap rallies at current price levels. With the Fed confirming a hold stance, physical demand from emerging market central banks running above 2025 pace, and both metals showing a clean technical base, Steer contends the next major upswing is imminent and that retail investors waiting for confirmation will miss the best entry points.

headline: NOVO RESOURCES COMPLETES MAIDEN WYLOO ANTIMONY-SILVER DRILL — High-Priority Targets Tested; Q3 Follow-Up Mapping Underway (TSX: NVO)
snippet: Novo Resources Corp. (TSX: NVO) announced completion of its maiden drill program at the Wyloo Polymetallic Project in Western Australia's Gascoyne region, where the Wyloo SE prospect tested a known polymetallic vein system with elevated silver, antimony, arsenic, zinc, and lead values in soil geochemistry, with assays pending. High-grade stream sediment anomalies east of Wyloo SE require follow-up ground work, and Q3 2026 mapping, rock chip sampling, and soil sampling have been planned across the Vera prospect — advancing what could be a significant antimony-silver system at a time when China's export restrictions on antimony have driven prices above $38,000 per tonne.

headline: OROSUR EARNS 100% OF DESEADO MASSIF GOLD PROJECT — 560km2 El Pantano JV Spend Complete; Epithermal System Open in Argentina (TSX-V: OMI)
snippet: Orosur Mining Inc. (TSX-V: OMI) completed its two-phase US$3 million earn-in at the El Pantano gold-silver project in Santa Cruz province, Argentina, converting to 100% ownership of 560km² of granted licences in the Deseado Massif — the same belt hosting AngloGold's Cerro Vanguardia and Newmont's Cerro Negro — subject to a 2% NSR retained by the prior JV partner. Maiden drilling of 5,533 metres confirmed a rift-related low-sulphidation epithermal system with intervals including 18.0m at 0.46 g/t gold, providing early-stage vectoring data for a follow-up drill program designed to test higher-grade structural targets within the broader corridor.
